A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the addition of glycerol or glycerophosphoric acid to the semen diluent increased the oxygen consumption rate of spermatozoal cells, while glycerol was more effective than glycerophosphates.
the addition of glycerol (0.01 M) to the semen of cattle, sheep, goats, pigs, horses and rabbits increased oxygen consumption.

the addition of glycerol or phosphoglycerol to the semen extender stimulates the respiration of bull and ram spermatozoa, and that the motility of bull spermatozoa is not impaired by the addition of glyceryl monoacetate or glycerol to the extender.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the addition of glycerol or phosphoglycerol to sperm diluent can enhance the respiration and movement of sperm in domestic animals.

the addition of glycerol to sperm suspensions is a very useful tool for the preservation of sperm motility in vitro, and that the effect of glycerol on sperm motility is not limited to a single species.
glycerol and PG can be used as cryoprotectants for the cryopreservation of domestic animal spermatozoa.
